explanation: The Roman governor who had authority over Jesus during his trial.
A method of execution in which a person is nailed or tied to a cross, used by the Romans to punish criminals and rebels.
The Hebrew title for the Savior promised in the Old Testament, often translated as "Christ".
A crown made of thorns that was pressed onto Jesus' head during his suffering, symbolizing both pain and an ironic appointment as king.
Describes Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the Sanhedrin who feared God and took Jesus' body for burial.
A cave or stone-cut burial place where Jesus' body was laid after his death.
A seal used to secure the entrance to the tomb to prevent theft and ensure that the body was not moved until after Passover.
